- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overreacts to volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds too much upward bias after peaks, failing to recognize price pullback.
- Forecast lags true trend by 1–3 days, especially in downward moves — model reacts too slowly to market corrections.
- Model exhibits high sensitivity to recent high prices, overfitting to recent spikes and failing to adjust for structural mean reversion.
- In low-volatility periods, model underestimates true price, often by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to anticipate the drop until 2–4 days later — exhibits delayed reaction to negative shocks.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating short-term price swings and overestimating long-term trend.
